run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/fraud-detection since 2026-11-17T09:55:15Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: Observed: in the data available for otel-demo (Prometheus/trace/event data ends between 09:15:38 and 09:25:15, before the 09:55:15 alert start), the only error-status spans attributed to service fraud-detection are its client calls to the flagd dependency: span_name flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream and flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/ResolveInt with status_code STATUS_CODE_ERROR; its order-path spans (orders receive, orders process) carry STATUS_CODE_UNSET and no errors. The fraud-detection EventStream client spans (service.version 2.1.3) record error=true, otel.status_code=ERROR, rpc.grpc.status_code=4 with durations of about 594-602 s, and their child flagd server spans (service flagd, version v0.12.8) carry otel.status_description "stream closed due to server-side timeout" and rpc.grpc.status_code=4. The same signature appears for service ad (10 EventStream error spans with the same flagd description), so this is a flagd event-stream timeout pattern seen by multiple flagd consumers, not a fraud-detection-specific failure. All fault flags in the flagd-config ConfigMap (adFailure, cartFailure, paymentFailure, kafkaQueueProblems, recommendationCacheFailure, etc.) are defaultVariant "off", so fault-flag injection is not the explanation. The flagd Deployment runs flagd v0.12.8 with command /flagd-build start --port 8013 --ofrep-port 8016 --uri file:./etc/flagd/demo.flagd.json (no stream-timeout argument visible); fraud-detection (10 pods, Running, ready, 0 restarts) points at it via FLAGD_HOST=flagd, FLAGD_PORT=8013. Hypothesis: the RequestErrorRate alert is driven by this recurring flagd event-stream timeout being recorded as gRPC code 4 error spans on fraud-detection. The exact alert expression and the exact 0.0222 value at 09:55:15 could not be verified because the alerting rule was not returned and no telemetry in this Run covers the minutes before the alert.

claims.text: The only error-status span series for service fraud-detection are its flagd client calls: traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="fraud-detection",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"} exists for span_name flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream and flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/ResolveInt, while its order spans (orders receive, orders process) appear only with STATUS_CODE_UNSET.

fraud-detection's EventStream client spans (service fraud-detection, service_version 2.1.3) carry error=true, otel.status_code=ERROR and rpc.grpc.status_code=4 with durations of about 594-602 s, and their child flagd server spans (service flagd, service_version v0.12.8) carry otel.status_description "stream closed due to server-side timeout" together with rpc.grpc.status_code=4; trace bd06756e0c7d97b40a884e5dac7ffd05 shows the fraud-detection client span of 599,999,905 us and the child flagd span with that description.

The same flagd EventStream signature appears for service ad: 10 client spans of about 597-604 s with error=true, otel.status_code=ERROR and rpc.grpc.status_code=4, with child flagd server spans (v0.12.8) carrying "stream closed due to server-side timeout"; spanmetrics also show error counters for ad flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/ResolveBoolean and for recommendation's /flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream, so the stream timeouts are not specific to fraud-detection.

fraud-detection's order-path activity shows no error status: the sampled fraud-detection traces consist of 30 "orders receive" and 30 "orders process" spans with status not_recorded and no error rows, and spanmetrics record 77 spans each for orders receive and orders process over the window with STATUS_CODE_UNSET and no error series for those span names.

All 10 fraud-detection pods are owned by ReplicaSet fraud-detection-9fb7d885b and are Running with ready containers and restartCount 0 (e.g. fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-2m24l), and the only flagd pod flagd-58db7486bd-2plsx is Running with restart counts 0,0 and started 2026-11-17T09:01:09Z; no fraud-detection or flagd pod shows a crash, OOM or eviction.

fraud-detection is configured with FLAGD_HOST=flagd, FLAGD_PORT=8013 and KAFKA_ADDR=kafka:9092, and the flagd Deployment runs image ghcr.io/open-feature/flagd:v0.12.8 with command /flagd-build start --port 8013 --ofrep-port 8016 --uri file:./etc/flagd/demo.flagd.json, i.e. no stream-timeout or deadline argument is visible in the pod template.

The error-terminating party in the observed traces is the flagd server: the span that carries otel.status_description "stream closed due to server-side timeout" is service flagd with service_version v0.12.8, which is the flagd Deployment's flagd container image (ghcr.io/open-feature/flagd:v0.12.8), so the stream closure that fraud-detection records as rpc.grpc.status_code=4 originates in flagd, not in fraud-detection's order-processing code.

No flagd fault flag was enabled in the snapshot: the demo.flagd.json in ConfigMap flagd-config has every flag (adFailure, adHighCpu, adManualGc, cartFailure, emailMemoryLeak, imageSlowLoad, kafkaQueueProblems, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure) at defaultVariant "off".

The alert's value could not be reproduced from the observable data: at 09:20:15 the expression sum(increase(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="fraud-detection",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}[5m])) / sum(increase(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="fraud-detection"}[5m])) evaluated to 0, because each per-instance error counter had only a single sample, while the total-span increases at that instant were 4.86 for "orders process", 4.86 for "orders receive" and 0 for the flagd span names.

The telemetry available in this Run stops before the alert: the fraud-detection error-counter series' last sample is 2026-11-17T09:25:15Z, the sampled fraud-detection traces have data_as_of 2026-11-17T09:16:28Z, and the events snapshot spans 2026-11-17T09:14:34Z to 09:17:38Z, while the alert started at 2026-11-17T09:55:15Z.

The RequestErrorRate alert fires because long-lived fraud-detection flagd EventStream spans (and ResolveInt spans) are counted as errors: the flagd server closes each event stream with "stream closed due to server-side timeout" after roughly 9-10 minutes, the gRPC client records DEADLINE_EXCEEDED (rpc.grpc.status_code=4), and this recurring trickle of error spans keeps the service error ratio above the alert's "above 0" condition (reported 0.0222) even though order processing shows no errors.

An enabled flagd fault-injection flag (for example paymentFailure, cartFailure or adFailure) caused fraud-detection's error spans — rejected because every flag in the flagd-config demo.flagd.json is defaultVariant "off", and the observed error description is a server-side stream timeout, not a flag-injected application failure.

Kafka problems caused fraud-detection's error rate — rejected as far as evidence goes: fraud-detection's Kafka order spans (orders receive, orders process) show no error status, and although kafka-ff7884766-lbw2w has 3 restarts and kafka-ff7884766-vg9vr has 1, no evidence ties those restarts to fraud-detection's flagd error spans.

Verify in the flagd Deployment/version whether the server-side event-stream timeout (which ends streams at roughly 9-10 minutes) and the clients' 600 s gRPC deadline are intended; if this is a known long-lived-subscription pattern, consider excluding flagd EventStream client spans from the RequestErrorRate numerator or requiring a minimum error count, and re-check the alert against data covering 09:50-09:55.

gaps: All metrics, traces and events returned in this Run end between 2026-11-17T09:15:38Z and 09:25:15Z, before the alert start 2026-11-17T09:55:15Z; the 5-minute window that produced the reported value 0.0222 was not observable, and instant queries at 09:55:15 and 10:00:00 returned nothing.

The RequestErrorRate alerting rule and its expression were not returned by list_prometheus_rules (no alerting rules matched), so the exact numerator, denominator and threshold behind "above 0 (current: 0.02222222222222222)" are unknown.

Logs for fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-2m24l (containers wait-for-kafka, fraud-detection) and flagd-58db7486bd-2plsx (containers init-config, flagd, flagd-ui) returned 0 lines, so application-log evidence for the error spans and for flagd's stream handling is unavailable.

No error span for flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/ResolveInt of fraud-detection was returned by Jaeger (search with error=true returned nothing), so the error description of those ResolveInt error spans, which exist in spanmetrics, is unknown.

kube-state-metrics/cAdvisor series such as kube_deployment_status_replicas_ready and kube_pod_container_info returned nothing from Prometheus, so pod readiness and resource usage over time could not be checked; pod state is only the current Kubernetes API state.

No events involving fraud-detection or flagd were returned, and the events snapshot covers only 09:14:34Z-09:17:38Z; the reason for the kafka pod restarts (kafka-ff7884766-lbw2w 3, kafka-ff7884766-vg9vr 1) is unknown and is recorded as a gap, not as impact.

Whether the flagd server-side stream timeout is default behaviour of flagd v0.12.8 or a misconfiguration could not be verified: no timeout argument appears in the Deployment command, no timeout setting appears in any otel-demo ConfigMap, and flagd logs were unavailable.
No change-history integration is available in this Run, so a change that may have altered flagd or fraud-detection behaviour before the alert could not be checked.
next_steps: Inspect the actual RequestErrorRate rule (expression, window, threshold, for) in the Alertmanager/Prometheus configuration that produced the alert.

Review flagd event-stream timeout behaviour and client deadline settings in the flagd Deployment and the fraud-detection flagd client configuration, and check flagd server logs for the stream-close events.
Re-query Prometheus/Jaeger for the 09:45-09:55 window once data ingestion for that period is available, to confirm the error spans driving the 0.0222 value are the flagd EventStream/ResolveInt spans.
Decide whether long-lived flagd EventStream spans should count toward the service request-error-rate signal, or whether the alert should require a nonzero error count or a higher ratio.
